On Mon, Dec 12, 2022 at 10:33 AM Kimberley Lucas <[contact omitted]> wrote:
I noted this in Sr staff today and it sounds like Michael Chelius has more information.
Also. the Burmamission had been looped in over weekend and has provided feedback
high side as to whether Burma is appropriate for this or not. (l am guessing not given
point two below? but leaving that discussion to high side) An excerpt from their email
this morning flagging this meeting noted:
DDI/DRG Center and CPS (I think) are leading out on USAID's contribution to a Sub-
IPC on Engagement of Tech Companies and Atrocity Prevention. They have identified 8
countries (Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Zimbabwe, Democratic Republic of Congo,
Ethiopia, Mali and El Salvador) that will be narrowed down to five. The criteria is to
identify countries with the best fits to engage with tech companies to prevent and
mitigate mass atrocities where 1) there are upcoming Key Events that could create a
risk of violence or mass atrocities, and 2) where tech platform engagement could have
a mitigating impact on those risks.
Kimberley Lucas
USAID/Asia/EAP Burma Desk (& Acting Asia/EAP Director Dec 2-12)
USAID Asia Bureau/Office of East Asian & Pacific Affairs (EAP)

1. Garth and his State department counterpart will put forward five countries including Bangladesh and
Burmafor consideration to NSC with the caveat that additional consultation/approval is needed with
missions/embassies and regional bureaus. They will also recommend that NSC chooses one country
to focus on as a test case/proof of concept while watching the other four for possible engangement.
Other countries are Zimbabwe, El Salvador, and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
1. If missions agree, I think we should advocate for an Asia country to get selected, perhaps Burma
given the recent request from AA Schiffer regarding Burma elections.

In brief, we are looking to engage with Tech companies to prevent and mitigate mass
atrocities where 1) there are upcoming Key Events that could create a risk of violence or mass
atrocities, and 2) where tech platform engagement could have a mitigating impact on those risks.
We (USAID and State) have been tasked by the WWhite House to separately prepare a list of up
to five counties where we believe the USG can engage with tech companies to mitigate risks of
mass atrocities. We have been tasked to send this list to the White House by COB on
Tuesday 12/13. Both State and USAID pushed back that this is unreasonable, but the deadline
[opaque block]
